metadataReview.note: Philip de Novare's account, in La Monte's 1936 translation, has the Cypriot host march onto the plain below the Lombard camp besieging Dieudamor (identified in the translator's notes as the castle of St Hilarion) and come between that camp and the casale of Agridi 'at the foot of the mountain', where battle was joined; the translator's introduction dates the victory at Agridi to 15 June, and a footnote cites the Gestes and Eracles for 'Tuesday, the fifteenth of June'. The locator is the gazetteer point for the village of Agírda, which GeoNames also names Agridhi, used as a sector reference. The existing date is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: GeoNames 146856 (Agírda, feature code P.PPL; alternate names include Agridhi, Aghirda and Ağırdağ) publishes latitude 35.29742 and longitude 33.26805, rounded to [33.2681,35.2974]. Nominatim returns the Ağırdağ village boundary relation 16272303 (wikidata Q4692682) about 0.1 km away. The identification of the medieval casale with the present village rests on this gazetteer name link, not on excavation or survey; it is consistent with Novare's description, since the point lies about 2.0 km south-west of St Hilarion Castle (Nominatim relation 2740924, 35.3121991, 33.2810729) at the foot of the range. The point is a village reference for the plain between Agridi and the Lombard camp; it is not a surveyed battlefield, a troop position or the mountain path to Dieudamor. No accuracy radius is claimed.
